title: Coroner's jury probes man's death
article: A coroner's jury is probing the death of a man who died after being restrained and stunned with a Taser by Burnaby Mounties.

Terrance Brian Hanna, 51, died April 20, 2003, after struggling with police inside the bar at the North Burnaby Inn on Hastings Street. During the struggle, he told an officer he'd taken six grams of cocaine and two speedballs, a mixture of cocaine and heroin.
The jury heard yesterday that Hanna, a truck driver, was brandishing a knife and a hammer.
Const. Normandie Levas said Hanna was in the throes of psychosis.
"It did not look like he was in control of himself," said Levas.
When an officer spoke to him, Hanna lunged at him with the knife. Four Mounties tackled him and held him face down on the floor.
Levas and constables Denise Mowry and Suhail Chaudhry all told the three-woman, two-man jury that Hanna was extremely combative and five officers had trouble holding him down.
The Taser was used on Hanna's lower back when he refused to put his arms behind his back.
Before he died, he complained that he was hot and couldn't breathe. When placed on his side, he struggled harder so police returned him to the prone position.
